 October 29, 2026 
 Daylight saving time ends Sunday; fall back to Eastern Standard Time at 2 a.m.
 New England will return to Eastern Standard Time (EST) on  Sunday, Nov. 1, when, at 2:00 a.m., clocks must be set back one hour to 1:00 a.m. Each of ISO New England’s market applications is unique and will function differently during this transition. Here are the things market participants need to know to prepare.
 1.  Bids and offers that use uploads and downloads for the eMarket application follow ISO 8601 Date and Time format for XML submittals. This is explained in section 3.1.2 of the  eMarket Data Exchange Specification  document posted on the ISO website.
 The transition will cover 2026-11-01T00:00:00–04:00 through 2026-11-01T23:00:00–05:00. For example: the time (or hour) is represented in the format below. Note that the DateTime format includes the time zone indicator, and the example shows time in Eastern Standard Time.
 time=”2026-11-01T00:00:00-04:00″
time=”2026-11-01T01:00:00-04:00″
 time=”2026-11-01T01:00:00-05:00″ (extra hour) 
time=”2026-11-01T02:00:00-05:00″
—
—
time=”2026-11-01T22:00:00-05:00″
time=”2026-11-01T23:00:00-05:00″
 2.  Asset telemetry, hourly resource availability uploads/downloads via the DRMUI application must submit the extra hour as given below.
 Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) time format upload/download 
 The transition will cover 2026-11-01T00:00:00–04:00 through 2026-11-01T23:00:00–05:00. For example:
 2026-11-01T04:00:00Z (first five-minute interval)
….
2026-11-01T05:00:00Z
….
2026-11-01T06:00:00Z
….
2026-11-01T07:00:00Z
….
2026-11-02T03:55:00Z
….
2026-11-02T04:55:00Z (last five-minute interval of the day)
 Eastern Standard Time for upload/download 
 The transition will cover 2026-11-01, 00:00:00–04:00 through 2026-11-01, 23:55:00–05:00. For example:
 2026-11-01 00:00:00–04:00 (first five-minute interval) (starts with Eastern Daylight Time with 4 hours offset)
….
2026-11-01 01:05:00–04:00
….
2026-11-01 01:50:00–04:00
….
2026-11-01 01:55:00–04:00
….
2026-11-01 01:00:00–05:00 (fall back by an hour and goes to Eastern Standard Time with 5 hours offset)
….
2026-11-01 01:05:00–05:00
….
2026-11-01 01:10:00–05:00
….
2026-11-01 02:00:00–05:00
….
2026-11-01 03:00:00–05:00
….
2026-11-01 04:00:00–05:00
….
2026-11-01 05:00:00–05:00
….
….
….
2026-11-01 23:55:00–05:00 (last interval for the day)
 3.  Internal bilateral transactions and any meter readings that use uploads and downloads for the SMS application must have the extra hour represented as 2* (that is, “2” followed by an asterisk). The  Contract Upload File Formats , the  Internal Bilateral Download , and the SMD Metering Upload File Format documents on the ISO New England website contain the required formatting information.
 4.  MIS reports will present the extra hour as 02X.
 5.  NEXTT  and OATI’s eTag systems handle the time change differently. NEXTT UI displays date/time in America/New York time zone, while OATI eTag allows user to set the time zone (for example, EDT, or EST). NEXTT automatically displays the extra hour in the market user interface, labeled “02X.” NEXTT file upload/download and programmatic interface use GMT datetime, which is not subject to any EDT/EST change. Examples of a NEXXT transaction are shown below. In general, eTags should be created in Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) and cover 25 hours (11/01/2026 00:00 – 11/02/2026 01:00). However, if the transaction begins after the time change has occurred, create the eTag in EST and create the schedule in the normal manner.
 1. File upload/programmatic interface: NEXTT schema uses standard GMT date time, no special DST/EST expression (like repeating hour).
 …
<RT_DETAIL>
<RT_TRANSACTION_TYPE>SELF SCHEDULED</RT_TRANSACTION_TYPE>
<RT_INTERVALS>
<RT_INTERVAL>
<INTERVAL_BEGIN>2026-11-01T04:00:00Z</INTERVAL_BEGIN>
<INTERVAL_END>2026-11-01T05:00:00Z</INTERVAL_END>
<BID_MW>100</BID_MW>
<BID_PRICE xsi:nil= “true” />
</RT_INTERVAL>
<RT_INTERVAL>
<INTERVAL_BEGIN>2026-11-01T05:00:00Z</INTERVAL_BEGIN>
<INTERVAL_END>2026-11-01T06:00:00Z</INTERVAL_END>
<BID_MW>110</BID_MW>
<BID_PRICE xsi:nil= “true” />
</RT_INTERVAL>
<RT_INTERVAL>
<INTERVAL_BEGIN>2026-11-01T06:00:00Z</INTERVAL_BEGIN>
<INTERVAL_END>2026-11-01T07:00:00Z</INTERVAL_END>
<BID_MW>110</BID_MW>
<BID_PRICE xsi:nil= “true” />
</RT_INTERVAL>
</RT_INTERVALS>
…
</RT_DETAIL>
</TRANSACTION>
 2. NEXTT UI: Date and hours are displayed in America/New_York time zone (may differ from the customer’s local time zone). The repeat hour is labeled as 02X: 
 Additional information and examples of NEXTT file formats are available in the  Upload and Download File Format Protocols  document on the ISO New England website. All market participants are encouraged to test their upload files for  Nov. 1, 2026 , in the SMD Sandbox.
 6. Lastly, daily Wind Power Forecast Application (WPFA)/Solar Power Forecast Application (SPFA) data includes an extra hourly data point during the fall back transition, while hourly WPFA/SPFA data is unchanged.
 DLYWPFA/DLYSPFA normally contains 120 hourly data points (5 days × 24 hours). During the fall back transition, the repeated hour increases this count to 121.
 XML submissions are required to specify a time zone indicator to avoid confusion during the daylight savings transition periods. Messages omitting the time zones will fail validation and be rejected. All dateTime values retrieved from a database will be presented with the UTC time zone (conforming exactly to how the value is stored in the database). 2026-11-01T01:00:00-04:00   (first occurrence, DST)
 2026-11-01T01:00:00-05:00   (second occurrence, standard time)
 or 2026-11-01T05:00:00Z
 2026-11-01T06:00:00Z
 HRLYWPFA/HRLYSPFA always contains 48 hourly data points and is not affected by the fall back transition.
 These counts are the same whether timestamps are represented in EST/local time or GMT/UTC.If you have questions on the information above, please contact the Participant Support and Solutions Team at 413-540-4220 or  AskISO@iso-ne.com .
